description: Validation corpus for the memory_negation feature (config: memory_negation_enabled). Each negated fact is paired with a positive distractor stating the OPPOSITE, so retrieval must be negation-aware to separate them: a naive lexical/semantic retriever scores both members of a pair highly on a negation query. Run the memory-retrieval eval with memory_negation OFF vs ON; the ON run should raise recall on the negation + discrimination cases WITHOUT regressing the positive controls. Kept OUT of the gated golden (memory_retrieval_corpus.json) so it never perturbs that regression baseline.

fixtures.content: In staging, Redis is configured WITHOUT persistence; all data is in-memory and lost on restart.
The local Postgres connection does NOT use SSL; it runs over a trusted unix socket only.
The public metrics endpoint requires NO authentication and is exposed read-only.
Failed background jobs are NEVER retried automatically; a human must requeue them.
The CDN cache is never purged on deploy; entries expire only by their TTL.
The staging environment does not send real emails; all mail is captured by a local sink.
The embedder runs on CPU only; no GPU is used in the default deployment.
Nightly backups are stored unencrypted on the local disk.
In production, Redis persists to disk via AOF fsync every second and survives restarts.
The production Postgres connection enforces SSL with full certificate verification.
The admin endpoint requires both an API key and a bearer token for every request.
Failed payment webhooks are retried automatically with exponential backoff up to five times.
The asset cache is purged on every deploy so clients always fetch the newest bundle.
The production environment sends real emails through the SES transactional provider.
The reranker runs on a dedicated GPU in the default production deployment.
Nightly database snapshots are encrypted at rest with a KMS-managed key.
Application logs rotate daily and are retained for fourteen days.
All stored timestamps are in UTC regardless of the client locale.
The service requires Python 3.11 or newer for its typing features.
